posts.name: LewdDolphin21
posts.cooked:
I played Imbued Fire immediately, making sure I never dealt Absolute Zero cold damage unintentionally, but I had no need to deal him cold damage anyway. I played Grease Gun after a Primeval Eruption, but then realized Akash'bhuta couldn't deal herself damage with that out, so I just stalled a round instead of killing everything like I had originally planned. I played Subzero Atmosphere smartly, making sure not to destroy it during Akash'bhuta's play phase, and actually spared the team a lot of damage from Living Rockslides (actually, no Rockslide ever dealt damage, which was cool). The last round featured a lot of shenanigans, between K.N.Y.F.E.'s Incidental Contact comboing with Flawless Execution, Incidental Contact and Imbued Fire having Absolute Zero do damage twice on K.N.Y.F.E.'s turn, Hoarfire doing a lot of damage because of Absolute Zero hitting himself for fire three times, and finishing with Ra's Inferno also hitting Absolute Zero in addition to Akash'bhuta and all Primeval Limbs. She had started that round at 95 HP.

The only unfortunate thing was that Tempest could not deal damage after the second round, due to the annoying Brambles (though he was partially responsible for it, having thrown one into the stratosphere...).

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Fine.

 

Boy, I had a series of very close games that didn't quite make it.  In the second game, with only Mr. Fixer and KNYFE left (Fixer at 2HP, and KNYFE at 1HP) I thought I had it perfectly set up for the win. Char would be brought back by Tempest's incap power to clear the board of dmaged limbs and wipe out Akash'Bhuta. Turns out, I forgot to factor in that because Ra had recently been incapped, Imbued Fire was no longer in play. This did clear the board of limbs, but becasue of my brainfart, Akash'bhuta was left with 1HP. Then Char burned the heroes to a crisp. Ugh.

 

Watched LewdDolphin's video--the main difference between my play and his was that he had Tempest play Localized Hurricane to draw a bunch, which led to an Into the Stratosphere that I never saw in my games. That proves to be a BIG factor -- by gumming up the villain deck and making that Prison Riot/Primeval Eruption combo less scary (still scary, but less so).

 

Anyway, I finally beat it.

posts.name: robb8888
posts.cooked:
Near-Mint.  On my second try, I used LewdDolphins Imbued Fire + SubZero Atmosphere trick (side note:  I never had a chance to play SZA my first go-round; it never showed up), and ended up with everyone alive except Tempest.  He probably would have made it as well, but I used his power first round to play a bunch of one-shots, which really knocked down his HP.  

 

Fixer was the big disappointer this match.  I never got either of his big Akash-blasting weapons (Dual Crowbars or Jack Handle) into his hands, so he was reduced to 2- or 3-HP shots every round, except for the times he played Overdrive.  Not great contributions out of KNYFE, either, since she never got her Blade or Gauntlets in hand, but the Imbued Fire helped her damage a bundh.  Ra was the MVP, between playing Imbued Fire, then pulling out a coupled of IF/Staff-powered Scorched Earths, and one neat round where the Flesh of the Sun God allowed KNYFE to use Incidental Contact without hurting the heroes.

Powerhound_2000:

You can keep them all alive and still win.   Considering the damage being laid out I like keeping AZ alive.  

 

So how'd you pull it off?  I read the comments on the forum, but still tried to play my first game "straight," as if I didn't know what was coming.  Was actually doing so-so, maybe a chance of winning, until an environment play forced out an Entomb that I couldn't do anything about.  That killed 3 heroes and knocked the others down to 2HP and 1HP respectively, with Akash still at about 100 HP.    As it stands, killing off AZ to get rid of the environment play seems like the safest way to beat it.  The multiple shuffles seem to prevent any other consistent strategy – I never saw "Subzero Atmosphere," for example, so LewdDolphin's strategy was right out.
